what_they_turned_out_to_be:
Second set. The first was almost entirely one thing: dx depended on the column (+19.7 / -0.2 / -23.2) and dy on the row (+34.6 / +2.7 / -27.9), fitting a single 9.6% contraction of the arrangement toward the wheel's centre. That was a mistake upstream showing through -- tile_scale shrinks each tile about ITS OWN centre, so the pictures got smaller while the gaps between them grew by exactly what each tile lost, and the drag was closing those gaps again nine times by hand. It is now closed once, in MARGIN, which went from 14 to 33; see the reasoning there. These numbers were then re-dragged against that, and are a third the size.

What is left, measured: dx no longer has a column signal worth naming (+4.7 / +2.6 / -2.2, spread 6.9 px against the old 42.9). dy still has a row signal (+18.6 / +6.1 / +3.4), and it fits a uniform downward push of 9.1 px plus a 2.7% vertical stretch to a mean error of 3.0 px. See `measured`, which is recomputed on every save so this paragraph can be checked against it rather than trusted.

That uniform 9.1 px is the next thing that is arithmetic rather than judgement: it says the tiles sit about 9 px high over their acolytes, and OVERLAP is the constant that means that. It was NOT moved, and the reason matters -- OVERLAP moves the acolyte row while an offset moves the tile, so shifting it there would slide all nine tiles up within the wheel rather than leave the picture alone. It is a real change to the render, not a free refactor, and it was judged against the board as it really draws. Move it only with an eye on the result.
survives: a new tile version, and a change to MARGIN. The shapes come from metadata/duty_grid_shapes.json and the version only chooses which art is clipped into them, so A/B/C/D share these. MARGIN was verified rather than assumed: each tile's depth over its acolyte row is invariant under it to +0.0 px on all nine, because the row is derived from the tile's own unoffset outline and the two move together. Editing the traced shapes themselves is what would invalidate these.
note: Per-tile nudges so each tile sits on its acolyte row the way The City does. Judged by eye: see gen_tile_offsets.py for the three derivable rules that were tried and why each failed. Screen pixels at the wheel's real drawn size, positive = right / down.
method: dragged in ui/render/gen_tile_offsets.py against a frozen acolyte grid
units: screen px at wheel width 877.8; positive = right / down

measured._: computed by gen_tile_offsets.decompose on every save; do not edit by hand
measured.read_this_as: A strong column signal in dx or row signal in dy, or a large uniform_px with a small mean_error_px, means these are not nine judgements: something mechanical is being done nine times by hand and belongs in a layout constant. MARGIN was raised from 14 to 33 for exactly that.
